body.rationale: Start at the near-threshold rung in block 0. A witness at rung 3 would settle rungs 0-3 as SATISFIABLE within that block, while a refutation at rung 3 would settle rungs 3-4 as UNSATISFIABLE. Symmetry mode is chosen to improve exact search pruning on the first probe while keeping most of the shared budget for the other independent blocks.

The rung 3 refutation applies only within block 0, so rungs 3 and 4 are UNSATISFIABLE. Blocks are independent, so the next best action is to test the analogous threshold rung in a fresh block with the same exact symmetry mode that already completed cheaply once.

Two independent blocks have already refuted the 141-clause rung with symmetry at low cost. Because refutation propagates upward only within the same block, the most efficient next probe is the analogous 141-clause rung in block 2; a REFUTED result would settle rungs 13 and 14 for that block while preserving most of the shared budget.

Three analogous midpoint exact solves with symmetry have already exhausted quickly in blocks 0, 1, and 2. The independent remaining block 3 has no evidence yet, so target rung 18: a refutation there would immediately settle rungs 18 and 19 in that block while using a budget comparable to prior successful probes. The block 2 refutation at rung 13 also propagates to rung 14 and is added to the claim sheet.

Block 3 has a verified witness at rung 18, so by within-block monotonicity rungs 15, 16, 17, and 18 are SATISFIABLE. Rung 19 is the only unresolved rung in that block and cannot be inferred from the rung 18 witness, so an exact solve there can settle the block completely if it finishes.

Block 0 has UNSAT established at rungs 3 and 4 only. Solving rung 2 is the highest unresolved lower rung in that block: a witness would settle rungs 0-2 as SATISFIABLE, while a refutation would extend UNSATISFIABLE to rung 2. The remaining budget is ample for a symmetry exact solve based on prior exhausted searches.

Block 3 is fully settled by the witness at rung 18 and refutation at rung 19. Block 0 has its boundary partly pushed down to rung 2, while blocks 1 and 2 still have larger unresolved lower intervals. Rung 7 is the highest unresolved rung in block 1; a witness would settle rungs 5-7 as SATISFIABLE, while a refutation would at least settle rung 7 and strengthen the block's UNSAT boundary. Use exact solving with symmetry because all completed exact calls so far have been decisive and relatively cheap compared with the remaining budget.

Final claim sheet warrants: block 0 has exact_solve REFUTED at rung 2, so by within-block monotonicity rungs 2, 3, and 4 are UNSATISFIABLE; no witness/refutation establishes rungs 0 or 1. Block 1 has exact_solve REFUTED at rung 7, so rungs 7, 8, and 9 are UNSATISFIABLE; no witness/refutation establishes rungs 5 or 6. Block 2 has exact_solve REFUTED at rung 13, so rungs 13 and 14 are UNSATISFIABLE; no witness/refutation establishes rungs 10, 11, or 12. Block 3 has exact_solve WITNESS_FOUND at rung 18, so rungs 15, 16, 17, and 18 are SATISFIABLE; exact_solve REFUTED at rung 19 establishes rung 19 UNSATISFIABLE. Blocks are independent, so no cross-block propagation is used.

Start with a midpoint probe in block 0 to maximize possible monotone closure within that independent block. Rung 2 has ratio 4.267, which falls in the transition band where the selection rule tries local_search first. Use the first Luby budget slice. No evidence has been obtained yet, so no rung can be claimed.

No verdicts are entailed by the prior inconclusive probe at rung 2. Continue binary-search coverage across independent blocks: block 1's midpoint is rung 7, its ratio 4.267 is in the transition band where the selector tries local_search first, and the next Luby budget is 5769.

Continue the binary-search midpoint coverage in an untouched independent block. Rung 12 is block 2's midpoint and has ratio 4.267, which falls in the in-between band where the selection rule says to try local_search first. A witness here would close rungs 10-12 as satisfiable within block 2; an inconclusive result would not justify any claim.

Blocks 0-2 have already received midpoint probes, all inconclusive, and no closure is earned from inconclusive evidence. Block 3 has not yet been probed, so the next highest-value action is its current midpoint rung 17. Its clause/variable ratio is 4.267, which falls in the intermediate band where the selection rule tries local_search first; use the next Luby budget slice with no preprocessing mode change.

Follow the portfolio and algorithm-selection schedule: rung 1 has ratio 4.000, so local_search is preferred. A verified witness at rung 1 would close rungs 0 and 1 in block 0 by monotone downward closure, while an inconclusive result will not justify any claim. Use the next Luby budget quantum of 5769 checks.

No rung has earned a SAT or UNSAT claim yet: all prior local_search probes were inconclusive and do not support closure. Following the published portfolio schedule and per-rung algorithm selection, the next unsettled ratio-4.000 rung is block 1 rung 6, where local_search is still the selected first probe. This also keeps evidence balanced across independent blocks while using the next Luby budget slice.

No prior probe produced a verified witness or completed refutation, so no rung is settled and no monotone closure applies. Following the portfolio schedule and algorithm-selection rule, the next untried high-value probe is block 2 local-index 1, rung 11, with ratio 4.000, which calls for local_search. Use the next Luby budget quantum of 5769 checks.

Final call with no verified witnesses or completed refutations in any block. All prior probes were inconclusive local_search runs, which establish neither satisfiability nor unsatisfiability, so no monotone closure applies. Every rung remains unresolved under calibrated abstention.

Start with the cheapest satisfiability-producing probe on the top rung of block 0. A verified witness at rung 4 would license SATISFIABLE for rungs 0-4 by within-block monotone closure; failure would license nothing but would give the first obstruction evidence for that block.

The only evidence so far is an inconclusive local_search at rung 4 caused by exhausted search budget, which licenses no SAT/UNSAT claim. Under minimum escalation, the warranted next step on the active rung is L0: allocate more budget to the same tool, same rung, same encoding before reseeding, switching tools, preprocessing, or moving to another block.

No warrant has been earned: two exhausted local-search budgets at rung 4 produced no verified witness and cannot license UNSAT. Within block 0, a witness at highest rung 4 would settle rungs 0-4 by monotone closure, so rung 4 remains the best current target. L0 more-budget probing has been tried once after the initial miss; the cheapest warranted escalation is L1, another same-tool restart/reseed on rung 4 before switching to exact solving or changing representation.

No claim is licensed: three failed local searches on rung 4 establish neither satisfiability nor unsatisfiability. Because same-tool budget/restart attempts have already been tried on rung 4 without a witness, the cheapest warranted escalation is L2: switch tool class to exact_solve on the same rung and encoding.

Block 0 is now settled at its top rung only: the completed refutation at rung 4 licenses UNSATISFIABLE for rung 4, but does not propagate downward. Because blocks are independent, the cheapest evidence-producing move is to begin an analogous probe in an untouched block. exact_solve at rung 9 can produce either a verified witness or a completed refutation, while local_search can only establish satisfiability and has already been weak on the analogous top rung in block 0.

Claims are limited to completed refutations already earned in their own blocks. Rung 9 must be added because the log contains an exhaustive REFUTED result there. Blocks 2 and 3 remain wholly unevidenced, and the cheapest action likely to create a warrant is to repeat the exact solver on the hardest rung of a fresh block, since exact_solve closed the analogous top rungs 4 and 9 cheaply while local_search on rung 4 repeatedly licensed nothing.

Blocks are independent, and block 3 has no evidence. The highest rung in each prior block was settled cheaply by exact_solve under mode none, while local_search on a highest rung produced only inconclusive results. With two control decisions left and ample remaining budget, the cheapest evidence-producing action for the untouched block is an exact solve at rung 19; if refuted, it establishes that rung directly, and if a witness is found, it would close all lower rungs in block 3 by monotone closure.

Final call: no further action will be executed. Only completed refutations at rungs 4, 9, 14, and 19 license verdicts. Because monotone refutation closure applies only to higher rungs within the same block, and each refuted rung is already the highest rung of its block, no additional rungs inherit UNSATISFIABLE. No verified witnesses exist, so no SATISFIABLE claims are licensed.

Start with the middle rung of block 0. Because rungs are nested within the block, a witness at rung 2 would also settle rungs 0 and 1 as satisfiable, while a refutation at rung 2 would settle rungs 3 and 4 as unsatisfiable. Exact solving is the most informative first probe near the expected transition.

The verified witness at rung 2 in block 0 also satisfies lower rungs 0 and 1, so rungs 0-2 are now SATISFIABLE. The next best use of a decision is to probe the top rung of the same block: a witness at rung 4 would settle all remaining rungs in block 0, while a refutation would at least settle the hardest rung and bracket the transition.

Block 0 now also supports UNSATISFIABLE at rung 4 from the completed refutation. Blocks are independent, so the next best use of budget is to start a new block. Solving the highest rung in block 1 is high leverage: a witness would settle all five rungs in that block, while a refutation at least settles rung 9 and helps locate the transition.

Block 1's refutation at rung 9 now establishes rung 9 as UNSATISFIABLE. Blocks 2 and 3 still have no evidence; probing the top rung of an untouched block with exact_solve can settle that rung if refuted, and leaves enough budget and decisions to continue boundary-finding afterward.

Block 3 has no evidence yet. Solving its top rung is the highest-upside next probe: a witness would settle all five rungs in block 3 as satisfiable, while a refutation would at least settle rung 19 as unsatisfiable. Existing exact solves have completed well within 60000 checks, so this is likely to return a decisive result within budget.

Block 1 has only its top rung refuted. Solving rung 8 is the highest-leverage next probe in that block: a witness would certify rungs 5-8 satisfiable, while a refutation would certify rungs 8-9 unsatisfiable. Prior exact solves exhausted quickly, so a 60000-check limit is reasonable within the remaining shared budget.

Use the next decision on block 2's penultimate rung. Since rung 14 is already refuted, solving rung 13 can either prove rung 13 UNSAT as well or, if a witness is found, immediately certify rungs 10-13 SATISFIABLE within block 2. The latest block 1 witness at rung 8 also propagates downward, so rungs 5-8 are now claimed SATISFIABLE.

Final call: no further action. Claims use only verified witnesses/refutations and within-block monotonic propagation. A witness at a rung proves all lower rungs in the same block satisfiable; a refutation at a rung proves all higher rungs in the same block unsatisfiable. Blocks are independent, so no cross-block propagation is used. Complete claim sheet with warrants: rung 0 SATISFIABLE (block 0: witness at rung 2 propagates down); rung 1 SATISFIABLE (block 0: witness at rung 2 propagates down); rung 2 SATISFIABLE (block 0: verified witness at rung 2); rung 3 UNRESOLVED (block 0: between SAT rung 2 and UNSAT rung 4, no direct result); rung 4 UNSATISFIABLE (block 0: exhausted exact refutation at rung 4); rung 5 SATISFIABLE (block 1: witness at rung 8 propagates down); rung 6 SATISFIABLE (block 1: witness at rung 8 propagates down); rung 7 SATISFIABLE (block 1: witness at rung 8 propagates down); rung 8 SATISFIABLE (block 1: verified witness at rung 8); rung 9 UNSATISFIABLE (block 1: exhausted exact refutation at rung 9); rung 10 SATISFIABLE (block 2: witness at rung 13 propagates down); rung 11 SATISFIABLE (block 2: witness at rung 13 propagates down); rung 12 SATISFIABLE (block 2: witness at rung 13 propagates down); rung 13 SATISFIABLE (block 2: verified witness at rung 13); rung 14 UNSATISFIABLE (block 2: exhausted exact refutation at rung 14); rung 15 UNRESOLVED (block 3: only refutation at rung 19, which does not imply lower rungs); rung 16 UNRESOLVED (block 3: only refutation at rung 19, which does not imply lower rungs); rung 17 UNRESOLVED (block 3: only refutation at rung 19, which does not imply lower rungs); rung 18 UNRESOLVED (block 3: only refutation at rung 19, which does not imply lower rungs); rung 19 UNSATISFIABLE (block 3: exhausted exact refutation at rung 19).

Start with block 0 midpoint to localize its boundary; rung 2 is in the in-between ratio band, so algorithm selection tries local_search first. This spends the first Luby slice and could prove rungs 0-2 satisfiable by within-block monotone closure if a witness is found.

No new verdict is entailed by the inconclusive rung 2 probe. Continue the midpoint sweep across independent blocks: rung 7 is block 1's current midpoint, has ratio 4.267 where the policy tries local_search first, and uses the next Luby budget slice.

No rung has earned a claim yet: the two prior local-search probes were inconclusive and do not establish satisfiability or unsatisfiability. To keep evidence balanced across independent blocks and follow the per-rung algorithm selection rule, probe the next untouched binary-search midpoint in block 2. Rung 12 has ratio 4.267, so the in-between region calls for local_search first, using the next Luby restart budget.

Probe the only block whose midpoint has not yet been tried. Rung 17 is the binary-search midpoint for block 3, its ratio 4.267 is in the transition band where the policy tries local_search first, and the next Luby allocation is 5769. No prior evidence establishes any satisfiable or unsatisfiable closure in any block.

No rung is settled yet. The midpoint local-search probes at ratio 4.267 were inconclusive in all four independent blocks, so the next highest-value move is to follow the portfolio schedule and algorithm-selection rule at a lower-ratio rung. Rung 1 in block 0 has ratio 4.000, where local_search is preferred; a verified witness there would close rungs 0 and 1 as satisfiable within block 0. Use the next Luby budget quantum, 5769 checks.

No verified witness or completed refutation has been obtained, so no rung can be claimed by version-space entailment. The next highest-value unsettled probe follows the portfolio schedule in a fresh block at ratio 4.000, where algorithm selection prefers local_search; use the next Luby budget quantum.

No rung has earned a satisfiable witness or completed refutation, so no claim is entailed. Following the published portfolio, rung 11 is the next unprobed ratio-4.0 rung in block 2; local_search is selected for ratio <= 4.12, with the next Luby budget quantum of 5769 checks. A witness there would close lower rungs 10 and 11 within block 2 only.

Final call: all executed probes were inconclusive and produced neither a verified witness nor a completed refutation. Monotone closure within blocks therefore has no source evidence to propagate, and independent blocks cannot share evidence. Every rung remains unresolved under calibrated abstention.

No evidence has been gathered yet, so no verdict is licensed. The cheapest informative first probe is local_search without preprocessing on a high-but-not-top rung in one block: a verified witness at rung 3 would monotonically settle rungs 0-3 within block 0, while an inconclusive result would justify same-rung budget/restart escalation before changing encoding or block.

The only evidence so far is an inconclusive local search at rung 3. That licenses no SAT/UNSAT claims. Minimum escalation requires L0 before changing tool, encoding, or rung: spend more budget on the same tool, same rung, same mode.

No verdict is licensed by the two inconclusive local-search attempts on rung 3. Because additional same-encoding local search has already been tried at increased budget without producing a verified witness, the cheapest justified escalation on the active rung is L2: switch tool class to exact_solve on rung 3. This rung is still a good pivot within block 0: a verified witness would close rungs 0-3 as SATISFIABLE by witness/monotone closure, while a completed refutation would close rungs 3-4 as UNSATISFIABLE by refutation/monotone closure.

The completed refutation at rung 3 licenses UNSATISFIABLE for rung 3 directly and for rung 4 by within-block monotone closure. Blocks are independent, so no claim transfers to blocks 1-3. Since rung 3 is settled, the cheapest useful escalation is to attack the analogous high-information rung in a new independent block with the tool class that just produced a completed refutation under budget.

Update claims first: the verified witness at rung 8 licenses SATISFIABLE at rung 8 directly and SATISFIABLE at lower rungs 5, 6, and 7 within block 1 by monotone closure. Blocks 2 and 3 have no evidence yet. The cheapest non-redundant next probe is to begin block 2 at its middle/high transition rung 13 with local search in the base encoding; this addresses SEARCH_INSUFFICIENT/PROBE_ACTION_INSUFFICIENT for an untouched independent block without spending exact-solve budget before a cheaper witness probe has been tried.

Rung 13 in block 2 has only had one inconclusive local-search attempt. That licenses no verdict, but the immediate obstruction is still SEARCH_INSUFFICIENT, so the minimum valid escalation is L0: more budget with the same tool, same rung, and same encoding. This also has good payoff if a witness is found, because it would close rungs 10-13 as satisfiable within block 2 by monotone closure.

Block 2 rung 13 has had two same-tool local-search budget increases without a witness. Since local_search cannot license unsatisfiability, the cheapest warranted escalation is L2: switch to exact_solve on the same rung and encoding. This can either verify a witness at rung 13, closing rungs 10-13 SAT by monotone closure, or complete a refutation at rung 13, closing rungs 13-14 UNSAT by monotone closure.
Final call: no further action will be executed. Claims are limited to verified witnesses, completed refutations, and monotone closure within each independent block only.

Start with the top rung of block 0. A verified satisfying assignment at rung 4 would settle all five rungs in that block as SATISFIABLE, giving the best possible propagation from one probe. No evidence exists yet, so no claims are added.

Use an exact probe at the middle rung of block 0. Because rungs are monotone only within a block, rung 2 is the best pivot: a witness would certify rungs 0-2 SATISFIABLE, while a refutation would certify rungs 2-4 UNSATISFIABLE. Symmetry mode is selected to maximize pruning under a bounded exact search. The prior local-search failure on rung 4 is not evidence strong enough to claim a verdict.

The verified witness at rung 2 settles rungs 0, 1, and 2 as SATISFIABLE within block 0 by subset monotonicity. Blocks are independent, so the next highest-value move is an exact solve on the middle rung of an untouched block; a witness would settle lower rungs in block 1, while a refutation would settle higher rungs.

Block 1 evidence was not yet propagated: REFUTED at rung 7 establishes UNSATISFIABLE for rungs 7, 8, and 9 within that block only. With block 2 still untouched, the best next high-leverage probe is the middle rung 12 under symmetry: either a witness settles rungs 10-12 SAT, or a refutation settles rungs 12-14 UNSAT, while staying within the remaining shared budget.

Block 3 has no evidence yet. Solving its middle rung maximizes propagation within that independent block: a witness would settle rungs 15-17 as satisfiable, while a refutation would settle rungs 17-19 as unsatisfiable. Existing block 2 evidence also propagates satisfiability to rungs 10-12.

Block 3 already has a verified witness at rung 17, so rungs 15, 16, and 17 are satisfiable. The remaining uncertainty in that block is rungs 18 and 19. Exact solving rung 18 is the best next probe: a refutation would also refute rung 19, while a witness would at least settle rung 18. This earns evidence within the block without relying on any cross-block inference.

Use an exact solve on block 2's first unresolved rung above a verified SAT rung. A witness at rung 13 would also settle rung 13 SATISFIABLE; a refutation at rung 13 would settle both rungs 13 and 14 UNSATISFIABLE. Also update block 3 by monotonicity: the completed refutation at rung 18 refutes rung 18 and higher rung 19 within that block.

Final claim sheet. Warrants: block 0 has a verified witness at rung 2, so rungs 0-2 are SATISFIABLE; rung 4 local search was inconclusive and gives no proof, so rungs 3-4 remain UNRESOLVED. Block 1 has a completed refutation at rung 7, so rungs 7-9 are UNSATISFIABLE; rungs 5-6 have no witness or refutation and remain UNRESOLVED. Block 2 has a verified witness at rung 12 and a completed refutation at rung 13, so rungs 10-12 are SATISFIABLE and rungs 13-14 are UNSATISFIABLE. Block 3 has a verified witness at rung 17 and a completed refutation at rung 18, so rungs 15-17 are SATISFIABLE and rungs 18-19 are UNSATISFIABLE. No cross-block propagation is used.

Start block 0 at its binary-search midpoint. Rung 2 has ratio 4.267, which is in the transition band where the prescribed algorithm selection tries local_search first. A verified witness here would close rungs 0-2 in block 0 by monotone SAT closure; inconclusive evidence will not change claims. Use the first Luby budget quantum.

The only new evidence is an inconclusive local search at rung 2, which entails no SAT/UNSAT claim and leaves every boundary position alive in block 0. To buy independent boundary information, probe the midpoint of another unresolved block. Rung 7 is block 1's midpoint, has ratio 4.267, and algorithm selection says to try local_search first in this transition band. Use the next Luby budget quantum, 5769.

Blocks are independent, so the two inconclusive midpoint probes in blocks 0 and 1 establish no claims and do not transfer to blocks 2 or 3. The next highest-value unsettled midpoint is rung 12 in block 2; its ratio is 4.267, which falls in the ambiguous band where the selection rule tries local_search first. Use the next Luby short-restart budget before escalating to exact solving.

Complete the first midpoint pass across the four independent blocks. Rung 17 is block 3's midpoint and has ratio 4.267, which falls in the in-between region where the selection policy tries local_search first. No prior evidence settles any rung in block 3, and no closure is available from the inconclusive probes in blocks 0-2.

Apply the portfolio schedule and skip rungs already settled by closure. Rung 16 is already settled by the verified witness at rung 17 in block 3, so the next unsettled scheduled probe is rung 1. Ratio 4.000 selects local_search, and the next Luby budget is 5769. The only new entailed claims so far are within block 3: a verified witness at rung 17 establishes rung 17 satisfiable and, by same-block monotone closure, rungs 15 and 16 satisfiable.

Use the current binary-search midpoint for block 3. Rung 18 is not settled by the witness at rung 17, has ratio 4.700 so algorithm selection favors exact_solve, and either possible completed outcome buys monotone closure within that block: a witness would add rung 18 SATISFIABLE, while a refutation would add rungs 18 and 19 UNSATISFIABLE. Existing inconclusive local-search probes in blocks 0-2 do not justify claims, so their claim states remain unresolved.

Block 3 is fully localized: the witness at rung 17 gives SAT for rungs 15-17, and the completed refutation at rung 18 gives UNSAT for rungs 18-19. Blocks 0-2 remain independent and unresolved. The midpoint local-search probes at rungs 2, 7, and 12 were inconclusive, so the next highest-closure move is to run an exact midpoint probe in one still-open block; rung 2 is symmetric with rungs 7 and 12 and is chosen first. A SAT result would close rungs 0-2 in block 0, while a REFUTED result would close rungs 2-4.
Final call: no further probes are available. Claims are limited to verified witnesses, completed refutations, and valid within-block monotone closure only; independent blocks do not share evidence.

No evidence exists yet. The cheapest first probe is local search on the highest rung of one block, because a verified witness there would license SATISFIABLE for all lower rungs in that block by monotone closure. This establishes evidence without claiming anything from absence of search results.

The only active evidence is an inconclusive local search on rung 4. That licenses no verdict. Under minimum escalation, the cheapest warranted response is L0: more budget with the same tool, same rung, and same encoding before changing tool class, preprocessing, or target rung.

Rung 4 in block 0 has had two same-encoding local-search attempts with no verified witness. That licenses no verdict, but it does exhaust the cheaper L0/L1 search probes on the current rung. The minimum warranted escalation is L2: switch tool class to exact_solve on the same rung and encoding, so the campaign can either verify a witness or possibly earn a completed refutation.

Update claim sheet with the only licensed new verdict: rung 4 is UNSATISFIABLE by COMPLETED_REFUTATION. Because blocks are independent, that establishes nothing in blocks 1-3. The next cheapest evidence-producing move is to use exact_solve on the top rung of a fresh block: local_search cannot certify UNSAT, and the analogous top rung in block 0 was cheaply refuted by exact search after local search failed.

Blocks 0 and 1 each produced completed refutations at their hardest/top rung with modest exact-solve cost after local search failed to prove anything. Blocks 2 and 3 still have no evidence at all, and a completed refutation must be earned independently inside each block. The cheapest warranted escalation that addresses the current obstruction is to apply the same exact solver at the top rung of an untouched block, where prior analogous blocks suggest a good chance of closing the rung within the remaining budget.

Completed refutations at rungs 4, 9, and 14 license only those rungs directly; because each is the highest rung in its block, no higher-rung monotone UNSAT closure is available. Rung 14 is added to the claim sheet because the log records a completed refutation there. The remaining entirely unprobed block is block 3, so the cheapest warranted action that earns independent evidence in that block is to apply the same exact solver configuration that has already exhausted the top rung cheaply in blocks 0-2.

Rung 19 has a completed refutation and must be added to the claim sheet. The remaining unsettled rungs are lower rungs in already-refuted blocks; top-rung refutations do not propagate downward. The cheapest decisive next probe is to attack the next lower rung in one block with the already-successful exact solver and unchanged encoding. Rung 3 is the immediate frontier below block 0's refuted top rung; a witness would close rungs 0-3 as SAT by monotone closure, while a completed refutation would close rung 3 directly.

Final call: no further action will be executed. Claims are limited to direct completed refutations and valid within-block monotone consequences only. Completed refutations at maximal rungs do not license lower rungs, and blocks are independent.

Start with the top rung of block 0. A witness here would settle all five rungs in this block as SATISFIABLE by monotonicity, while a refutation would at least settle the hardest rung as UNSATISFIABLE. Allocate roughly one quarter of the shared budget so the four independent blocks can each receive comparable evidence.

The completed refutation at rung 4 only establishes UNSATISFIABLE for block 0 rung 4; it gives no information about lower rungs or other blocks. With substantial budget remaining and only 7 control decisions left, the highest rung of an untouched block is the best next probe: a witness would settle all five rungs in that block as SATISFIABLE, while a refutation at least settles the hardest rung and tests whether the block-0 pattern repeats.

Two independent top rungs have already refuted cheaply under symmetry, but block evidence does not transfer across blocks. The best next use of shared budget is to test the top rung of an unexamined block; a refutation at rung 14 would settle the hardest rung in block 2, while a witness would settle all lower rungs in that block by subset monotonicity.

Three independent blocks have already been refuted at their highest rung with symmetry exact solving at modest cost. Block 3 has no evidence yet, so the highest-value next action is to attempt the same highest-rung refutation there. The prior refutation of rung 14 should also be added to the claim sheet; it only establishes rung 14 within block 2, not lower rungs.

Block 0 has only the top rung refuted, which establishes rung 4 only. Solving the middle rung 2 is the highest-leverage next probe in that block: a witness would settle rungs 0-2 as SATISFIABLE, while a refutation would settle rungs 2-4 as UNSATISFIABLE. The latest log also establishes rung 19 as UNSATISFIABLE, which was missing from the claim sheet.

Propagate the new block-0 witness: rung 2 is satisfiable, so rungs 0 and 1 are also satisfiable within block 0. Rung 3 remains the only unsettled rung in block 0. With three decisions left and all blocks independent, the best next probe is an exact solve at a middle rung of another block; rung 7 can either prove SAT for rungs 5-7 or UNSAT for rungs 7-9.

Blocks 0 and 1 already show satisfiability at the 128-clause rung and unsatisfiability at the 168-clause rung, leaving the 141-clause boundary as the highest-value probe. In block 2, solving rung 13 can settle four rungs if a witness is found (10-13 SAT by downward closure), and still settles rung 13 if refuted. The remaining budget supports a 75000-check exact solve while preserving budget for one final decision.

Final claim sheet. Warrants by block monotonicity: block 0 has a verified witness at rung 2, so rungs 0-2 are SATISFIABLE; rung 4 was REFUTED, so rung 4 is UNSATISFIABLE; rung 3 has no direct witness or refutation. Block 1 has a verified witness at rung 7, so rungs 5-7 are SATISFIABLE; rung 9 was REFUTED, so rung 9 is UNSATISFIABLE; rung 8 has no direct witness or refutation. Block 2 has REFUTED results at rungs 13 and 14, so rungs 13-14 are UNSATISFIABLE; rungs 10-12 have no direct witness or refutation. Block 3 has rung 19 REFUTED, so rung 19 is UNSATISFIABLE; rungs 15-18 have no direct witness or refutation. Blocks are independent, so no cross-block propagation is used.

Probe the midpoint of block 0 first to maximize possible monotone closure within that independent block. Rung 2 has ratio 4.267, which is in the crossover band where the prescribed selector tries local_search first. Use the first Luby budget quantum.

No rung has been settled: the prior local search on rung 2 was inconclusive and cannot support either satisfiability or unsatisfiability. To buy independent evidence across blocks while following midpoint probing, move to block 1's midpoint rung 7. Continue the binary-search midpoint coverage across independent blocks. Blocks 0 and 1 midpoint probes were inconclusive, so they establish no closure. Rung 12 is block 2's current midpoint; its ratio 4.267 is in the transition band where the selection rule says to try local_search first. Use the next Luby budget quantum, 11538 checks.

Rung 17 is block 3's current binary-search midpoint with ratio 4.267, which falls in the transition band where the prescribed algorithm selection tries local_search first.
